title: Last Moment Before All Ants Fall Out of a Plank
statement:
A plank runs from position `0` to position `n`. Ants stand at distinct integer positions on it: every ant listed in `left` walks toward `0`, every ant listed in `right` walks toward `n`, and all of them cover 1 unit per second. Whenever two ants heading toward each other meet, both turn around instantly and keep walking. An ant that arrives at either end at time `t` drops off at that very moment (an ant already at the end it faces drops off at time `0`).

Return the time at which the final ant drops off the plank.
constraints: Every position appears at most once across left and right together
signature: int getLastMoment(int n, int[] left, int[] right)
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating every turn-around is messy. But ants look identical, so when two of them meet and both reverse, the picture is exactly the same as if they had walked straight through each other and swapped name tags. With that view no collision ever changes anything: each "walker" just keeps its original direction until it drops off. A left-walker at `p` needs `p` seconds, a right-walker at `p` needs `n - p` seconds, and the answer is the largest of those times.

## Approach

1. Start `last` at 0.
2. For each `position` in `left`, the walker needs `position` seconds to reach 0; keep the maximum in `last`.
3. For each `position` in `right`, the walker needs `n - position` seconds to reach `n`; keep the maximum.
4. Return `last`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 4`, `left = [4, 3]`, `right = [0, 1]`.

- Left-walkers: `position = 4` gives `last = 4`; `position = 3` leaves it at 4.
- Right-walkers: `position = 0` needs `4 - 0 = 4`, `position = 1` needs `3`; `last` stays 4.

The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L + R): each ant is looked at once.
- Space: O(1): only the running maximum is kept.

## Pitfalls

- Do not simulate the bounces: it is slow and easy to get wrong when ants meet halfway between integer points.
- A right-walker's time is `n - position`, not `position`.
- Either array may be empty, so start `last` at 0 rather than reading the first element.
- An ant already at the end it faces drops off at time 0, which the formulas handle naturally.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `last` | the latest drop-off time found so far |
| `position` | the starting position of the current ant |

narration.2: No ant has fallen yet, so the latest drop-off time starts at 0.
narration.4: Treat colliding ants as passing through each other: each left-walker keeps walking toward 0.
narration.5: A left-walker at this position needs exactly that many seconds; keep the largest.
narration.8: Each right-walker keeps walking toward n.
narration.9: It needs n minus its position seconds to reach the right end; keep the largest.
narration.12: The slowest walker determines when the plank becomes empty.
